$comment: A host's policies, which come with every call, as docs/engine-hosts.md#what-a-host-decides lists them. A policy left out takes its default, NexKit 6's on GitHub without autopilot, except `parentEnd`, which keeps the engine's rule (GitHub's `close_parent_issues` is off by default). These are the policies the engine decides with.

fixRounds.$comment: How many fix rounds run before a person decides, from 0 to 10.

conflictRounds.$comment: How many rounds may resolve or redo conflicts, when `conflicts` is resolve or redo, from 1 to 10.

splits.$comment: Whether an approved plan that is too large and names its parts is split into them.

answers.$comment: With automatic approval, whether the engine answers a plan's questions with their recommended options when every question has one, at most once in a row; otherwise a person answers them.

afterFailure.$comment: What follows a failed round that has nothing for a person to answer. Under `replan`, an item that failed because its round was blocked with nothing to answer, on no change, is planned again after a person's comment or a blocker's close; the GitHub host sends `replan` with autopilot.

splitParts.$comment: The most parts a split files, from 1 to 10; with automatic approval a plan with more is planned once more for fewer, and a person's approval of one goes on as one change.

splitDepth.$comment: How deep parts go, from 1 to 10: the item first split is at depth 0, and an item at this depth is not split again.

parentEnd.$comment: Whether a split parent ends when its parts did: whenPartAccepted ends it as accepted once every part ended and one was accepted, and person leaves it to a person (splitIncomplete). Only a split parent reads it, so a round's stored policies leave it out. A host that leaves it out gets the first; the GitHub host sends person when `close_parent_issues` is off.

retryWaits.$comment: The waits in minutes before an agent run that stopped on a transient error runs again, one for each run again, at most 10, each from 0 to 330; a wait of 0 runs it again at once, and after the last a person decides.

lostWaits.$comment: The waits in minutes before an agent run or checks that the engine started by itself and the host lost start again, one for each start again, at most 10, each from 0 to 330; a wait of 0 starts them again at once, and after the last a person decides. The engine reads it as the host gives it at each loss and never keeps it. The default, none, fails a lost action for a person.

budgets.$comment: What each stage's agent run may spend, by stage (`triage`, `plan`, `implement`, `fix`, `review`): tokens, seconds and model calls, each from 1, or null for no limit, and no money. `item` limits one work item across all its stages and rounds: its tokens count every run as input plus output, and its seconds count from `used.since`. The engine caps each implement, fix and review run's budget by what is left, and fails the item when either runs out. The engine copies the stage's into each `runAgent.budget`, `modelCalls` only when it is set, and reads `budgets` as the host gives it at each step and never keeps it. A limit on one session is the runner's to enforce, as docs/engine-hosts.md#runners says.

agents.$comment: The agent, model and effort of each stage's run, by stage (`triage`, `plan`, `implement`, `fix`, `review`), each a string or null for the runner's own choice. The engine copies the stage's values into each `runAgent` and gives null for a value the host leaves out. It reads `agents` as the host gives it at each step and never keeps it. An agent's fallbacks are the runner's: it runs them in turn within the one action, as docs/engine-hosts.md#runners says.
